instructions: Wash the apples, cut them in half and cut out the cores.
Slice each half into wedges, or cut the apples crosswise into rings about 1/4 inch thick.
Spoon the sunflower seed butter into a small bowl and put it in the middle of a plate.
Fan the apple slices around the bowl. Dip each slice or spread the butter on with a knife.
For a lunch box, pack the sunflower butter in a small container beside the apple slices. Cut the apples the same morning you eat them.
method_notes: SunButter's apple sandwich page is the only published version that matches this snack by name: apple slices cored and sliced into rings, spread with sunflower seed butter. It has no rating and gives no amounts, so the amounts here are for three apples and a half cup of butter, and its granola and chocolate chips are left out. Sunflower seed butter is the usual nut-free swap for peanut butter, but check the jar for a nut-free label. Super Fresh Growers' sunflower seed dip is a related idea (a thinned seed butter dip) but adds almond milk, so it is not used.
